label: Learning map
title:
Let internal learning
preserve the faint signal.
lede: From Mamba representations to TTT inner and outer loops for single-frame infrared small-target detection. TTA papers remain conceptual comparisons; visual TTT is the experimental focus.
body:
Understand the TTT inner loop ↗Weekly replication matrix →

Place the research question at the right level

Our working hypothesis is that the group baseline uses TTT as a visual sequence-modeling module. Its paper and implementation still need confirmation; neither a name nor a 76.x score identifies a model. Mamba/VMamba provide representation references, while Tent, CoTTA and SAR address a different adaptation setting.

01 / MECHANISM

A small model as state

Adjust a gradient step and distinguish inner weights W, outer parameters θ, queries and outputs.

TTT mechanisms →
02 / VISION

From token order to a spatial grid

Why causal scans, position encoding, CLS tokens and dense outputs require new choices.

From text to vision →
03 / IRSTD

Replicate, then test one change

Original and prototype variants, a local-detail hypothesis, accuracy and full computational cost.

Experiment matrix →

Choose a route for today

GoalReading orderTakeaway
A 30-minute frameworkTTT → text to vision → IRSTDUpdate targets, sequence and outputs
Prepare replicationWeekly plan → paper index → relevant mechanismAn exportable draft and configuration checklist
Build backgroundFoundations → Mamba → VMamba; read TTA separatelyRepresentation modules versus domain adaptation
Teaching and research boundaries

This site runs no neural-network training and invents no detection scores. Scalar learning traces follow explicit toy equations. IRSTD changes are hypotheses; the colleague’s prototype design is not a new contribution from this site.

Course scope

13 pages, 11 learning units and 8 interactive demonstrations. ViT³ and Vision-TTT connect TTT work from 2024–2026; original TTT 2020, Tent 2021 and CoTTA 2022 remain background. Progress and notes stay in the current browser.

Foundations · Mamba · Primary sources

label: 01 Foundations
title:
First, distinguish:
what exactly is learning?
lede: Architecture, inference state, and test-time optimization are three different levels. Separating them clarifies the research questions behind Mamba + TTA/TTT.
body:
The same “test time,” four different kinds of change

MechanismWhat changesAre gradients computed at test time?Is it retained across images?
Mamba / VMambaScan hidden state h; network parameters are usually fixedNot required for standard inferenceUsually only within the current image's scan
TTA methods such as Tent / CoTTAModel parameters θ, statistics, or teacher parameters φRequired by these methodsDetermined by the episodic / continual protocol
Original TTT (2020)A self-supervised task updates shared feature parametersYesCan reset for each sample or persist online
TTT layers（2024/2025）Small-model weights W inside a layer, serving as the hidden stateInner-loop gradients are part of the forward computationDetermined by the sequence definition and state boundaries

Original sources: Mamba · COLM 2024 / arXiv 2023 ↗ · Tent · ICLR 2021 ↗ · Original TTT · ICML 2020 (conceptual background) ↗ · TTT layers · ICML 2025 / arXiv 2024 ↗

Disambiguating the abbreviation

Here, TTA means Test-Time Adaptation. Test-Time Augmentation is also abbreviated TTA, but averaging predictions over multiple views does not necessarily update parameters.

Mathematical objects for the current task

Training set Dtrain = {(xᵢ,yᵢ)} → outer learning of θ
One image x → spatial tokens → inner updates of W → dense features z
pθ,W(x) ∈ [0,1]H×W → thresholds and connected components → target positions

Training masks supervise the outer task. The inference-time inner objective is built from current image features and receives no test mask. Outer parameters are usually fixed; inner states are initialized and updated at image/layer boundaries. Follow the selected baseline for projections, losses, ordering and reset rules.

A single-frame task does not require state to persist across images. We first study representation computation within each image. Direct cross-dataset testing is a separate generalization evaluation and does not automatically add adaptation updates.

TTT is the project’s starting route

Current focus: TTT as representation

Attach original TTT to a fixed segmentation decoder, compare the prototype variant, then test one IRSTD-specific change. Source training or fine-tuning is needed; focus on tokens, inner models, objectives and dense outputs.

Understand the two loops →

Conceptual comparison: test-domain adaptation

Tent/CoTTA update selected parameters from test inputs. Their mechanisms and failure examples remain in the course, but they are not the project’s default next experimental stage.

See the current experiment matrix →

Prerequisites in four sentences

Gradient: the local rate of change of loss with parameters; a negative-gradient step may reduce loss without improving task correctness. Entropy: prediction uncertainty, not truth or falsehood. State: a compressed memory of inputs already seen. Pseudo-label: supervision generated by the model itself, which may propagate errors.

Pause and test your intuition

If h evolves while VMamba processes a new image, does that alone demonstrate TTA?

label: 02 Mamba principles
title:
Write memory as a recurrence,
then let the input decide what matters.
lede: Mamba is about more than linear complexity. What gets written into the state, what is retained, and how is it read out?
body:
Paper mechanism: from a continuous system to a discrete sequence

dh(t)/dt = A h(t) + B x(t)　　y(t) = C h(t) + D x(t)
A̅ = exp(ΔA)　　B̅ = [∫₀Δ exp(sA) ds] B
hₜ = A̅ₜ hₜ₋₁ + B̅ₜ xₜ　　yₜ = Cₜ hₜ + D xₜ

h is compressed memory; A controls the dynamics, B writes, C reads, D is the input feedthrough term, and Δ sets the scale of one evolution step. Zero-order-hold discretization assumes a constant input within each sampling interval; when A is invertible, B̅ = A⁻¹(exp(ΔA) − I)B.

Mamba makes Δ, B, and C input-dependent, replacing fixed filtering with content-dependent selection. Not every parameter is generated token by token: A in the basic formulation remains a shared learned parameter. The ΔB input term commonly used in implementations is a simplification, not the exact general zero-order-hold solution.

Original sources: Mamba · COLM 2024 / arXiv 2023 ↗

Teaching demo: how long can a target impulse persist?

A = −1，B = C = 1，D = 0：
a = exp(−Δ)，hₜ = a hₜ₋₁ + (1−a)xₜ

Increasing a retains the old state longer but writes the current impulse more weakly; decreasing a strengthens the new input while forgetting faster. An impulse may be a true target or defective-pixel noise, so longer memory is not automatically better or worse.

How can a recurrence still be parallelized?

(a₂,b₂) ∘ (a₁,b₁) = (a₂a₁, a₂b₁+b₂)

Each step is an affine transformation hₜ=aₜhₜ₋₁+bₜ. Composition is associative, enabling a parallel prefix scan. Input-dependent parameters cannot directly become a fixed convolution, making hardware-aware implementation crucial for efficiency.

With channel count and state dimension fixed, computation grows linearly with sequence length L. This does not mean independence from network width or guarantee that every CPU/GPU implementation is fast.

Mamba-2: why read about SSD?

Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality (ICML 2024) introduces SSD by using structured matrices to connect a class of SSMs with attention computation. It helps you see recurrence and blockwise matrix operations as different organizations of the same computation.

The title does not imply that arbitrary softmax Transformers and arbitrary SSMs are fully equivalent. Speedups in a language model's core layer do not directly translate into end-to-end IRSTD speedups: backpropagation, teacher forward passes, and the decoder can all become bottlenecks.

Original sources: Mamba-2 / SSD · ICML 2024 ↗

IRSTD research hypothesis

Global memory may help determine whether a bright point belongs to a cloud edge or structured background; a finite-dimensional state may also compress away weak targets. Examine shallow details, metrics stratified by target size, and local pathways, rather than reporting only whole-image IoU.

Pause and test your intuition

What happens when Δ increases in the scalar demo?

label: 03 VMamba close reading
title:
Turn a two-dimensional image
into four directional readings.
lede: VMamba: Visual State Space Model · NeurIPS 2024. Understand SS2D indexing, merging, and hierarchical structure to judge what it preserves for tiny targets.
body:
Paper mechanism: SS2D's four routes are not four straight lines

The feature map X∈ℝH×W×C is flattened into four complete sequences: row-major, column-major, and their reversals. Each route performs a selective scan, then maps back to the original pixel coordinates before merging. Every route visits all H×W positions.

X → row-major / column-major / reversed row-major / reversed column-major
Each route: selective_scan → inverse_permutation
Align to the same (i,j), then merge → Y

Original sources: VMamba · NeurIPS 2024 ↗

From SS2D to a vision backbone

The final NeurIPS VSS block combines LayerNorm, SS2D, an FFN, and residual connections and is stacked into a hierarchical backbone. Hierarchical representations can feed a dense-prediction decoder, but global semantics and original-pixel localization are different objectives.

Read the scan in Figure 2 and the final block in Figure 3, and pin the official code version. Details such as gating changed between the early preprint and the final version; the architecture diagram should match the version actually reproduced.

Multidirectional scans are complementary, but neither strictly rotation-invariant nor able to preserve all two-dimensional adjacencies. Consecutive sequence positions may cross from the end of one row to the start of the next.

Original sources: VMamba · NeurIPS 2024 ↗

A 3×3 target enters the backbone: three checkpoints

LocationWhat may be lostHow to check
Input and patch embeddingSubpixel contrast and bright-point peaksCompare target pixels before and after resizing; fix the interpolation method
Multistage downsamplingSpatial position and local boundariesRetain shallow skip connections; stratify misses by target area
Scanning and fusionWeak signals in a finite stateCompare local branches and one/four routes while controlling computation
Check normalization layers before attaching Tent

VSS blocks mainly use LN. The standard original Tent implementation selects BN affine parameters and re-estimates batch statistics; applying it unchanged may collect no parameters. Updating LN's γ and β should be called an “LN-affine entropy variant.” The decoder may contain additional BN, so inspect the actual model.

A minimal parameter-inspection approach
# Illustration, not a complete reproduction of Tent
for name, module in model.named_modules():
    if isinstance(module, (BatchNorm2d, LayerNorm, GroupNorm)):
        print(name, type(module).__name__)
# Explicitly check trainable parameter names, counts, and nonzero gradients.
# Reset the model, optimizer, teacher, statistics, and cache.

Pause and test your intuition

Why apply an inverse permutation before merging SS2D outputs?

label: 04 Tent close reading
title:
Why can reducing uncertainty
also reinforce mistakes?
lede: Tent: Fully Test-Time Adaptation by Entropy Minimization · ICLR 2021. A minimal adaptation objective and an entry point for understanding background collapse in IRSTD.
body:
The current route is internal learning with TTT

This chapter is retained as a TTA comparison, not the project’s experimental route. The current sequence is original TTT → prototype variant → one IRSTD-specific change. Start with TTT mechanisms or the replication matrix.

Paper mechanism: change only a small subset of parameters

L_ent = − (1/B) Σᵦ Σ꜀ pᵦ꜀ log pᵦ꜀
(γ, β) ← (γ, β) − η ∇γ,βL_ent

The source model is already trained, and neither source data nor target labels are accessed at test time. The classic BN setup uses target-batch statistics and optimizes channelwise affine γ and β while fixing most weights. The model constructs its update signal from its own prediction entropy.

This provides no calibration guarantee. Entropy asks how certain an answer is, not whether it is correct. Convolutional BN with batch=1 can still compute statistics over spatial dimensions; pixel correlation and background bias are the concerns, not a universal inability to compute statistics.

Original sources: Tent · ICLR 2021 ↗

Is your binary segmentation loss correct?

H(p) = −p ln p − (1−p) ln(1−p)，p=σ(z)
∂H/∂z = p(1−p) ln((1−p)/p)

For a single-channel sigmoid, include both foreground p and background 1−p. Computing only −p log p is incomplete; applying softmax over a single channel always yields 1, with zero entropy.

For an independent logit, p<0.5 is pushed lower, p>0.5 is pushed higher, and the gradient at p=0.5 is zero. Real networks share parameters, so each pixel's update is also influenced by other pixels.

Why are tiny targets especially vulnerable?

A 3×3 target in a 256×256 image occupies only about 0.0137%. Mean pixel entropy mainly reflects the background. If a weak target starts at p=0.4, entropy minimization may push it toward 0. Confident all-background predictions also have very low entropy.

The demo groups foreground pixels using toy ground truth

Real unlabeled adaptation cannot use the target mask to compute a foreground loss. Experimental candidates must come from predictions or unlabeled rules, and the risk of missing candidates must be diagnosed independently.

Build an honest baseline in your model

  1. Reproduce the frozen source model's segmentation and object-level metrics, and save θ₀.
  2. Inspect BN/LN and list the parameters actually updated and the optimizer state.
  3. Compare source-only and norm-affine entropy using the same checkpoint, without also changing the decoder.
  4. Fix the step count, learning rate, and output timing; report per-image resets and cumulative adaptation separately.
  5. Plot Pd, Fa, and entropy over samples, examining long empty-background stretches and target reappearance.

Pause and test your intuition

What does a decrease in mean entropy tell you?

label: 05 CoTTA close reading
title:
Give updates a memory,
and preserve a way back to the source model.
lede: Continual Test-Time Domain Adaptation · CVPR 2022. Separate teacher averaging, augmentation averaging, and stochastic restoration to see what each component addresses.
body:
The current route is internal learning with TTT

This chapter is retained as a TTA comparison, not the project’s experimental route. The current sequence is original TTT → prototype variant → one IRSTD-specific change. Start with TTT mechanisms or the replication matrix.

Paper mechanism: three roles and one update order

Source model θ₀ (fixed), student θ, teacher φ
q ← teacher prediction / augmentation average
θ ← θ − η∇θ CE(q, pθ(x))
φ ← α φ + (1−α) θ
θ ← M ⊙ θ₀ + (1−M) ⊙ θ，Mⱼ ∼ Bernoulli(r)

The frozen source model's confidence determines whether augmentation averaging is enabled. The teacher provides soft pseudo-labels for the student, followed by the EMA teacher update and finally stochastic restoration of some student parameters. Restoration replaces individual elements; it does not zero the entire model.

Specify which prediction is returned and whether it is produced before or after adaptation. Restoration does not retroactively change a prediction already returned in the current round.

Original sources: CoTTA · CVPR 2022 ↗

Two kinds of averaging, two different problems

ComponentWhat it smoothsWhat it cannot guarantee
EMA teacherParameter trajectories across stepsCannot correct shared biases
Augmentation averagingDifferences between views of the same inputCannot guarantee that augmentations preserve tiny targets
Stochastic restorationThe student's forgetting of source knowledgeMay not help when the source model performs poorly in the new domain

The old state's weight decays as αᵏ. Larger α gives more smoothing, but may respond more slowly after a sudden sensor change. This demo simulates EMA alone, not full CoTTA performance.

Reconsider augmentations for single-frame IRSTD

Strong cropping, resizing, and blurring may erase targets only 2–5 pixels across. Segmentation predictions from geometric augmentations must be inverse-transformed into common coordinates before consistency or averaging; cropping also requires handling the valid overlap region.

First use the labeled source validation set to check target retention and contrast changes, then fix the rules for unlabeled testing. Do not use target-test ground truth to decide whether an image is suitable for augmentation.

Continual does not require video

Detection remains single-frame, one image at a time; student, teacher, and optimizer states simply accumulate across images. NUAA→NUDT→NUAA can test domain switching and forgetting, but it is a controlled image sequence and cannot be described as exploiting real temporal continuity.

Start with a CoTTA-style variant

Fix the source Mamba model and begin with normalization parameters or a decoder adapter. Use teacher probability maps under weak augmentations for consistency supervision, adding EMA and stochastic restoration separately. If the updated parameters and augmentations change, explicitly call it a CoTTA-style variant, rather than a complete reproduction of the original paper.

Record the number of student forward passes, backward passes, and teacher forward passes. End-to-end latency captures the cost better than a single backbone inference.

Pause and test your intuition

Can an EMA teacher automatically eliminate pseudo-label errors?

label: 06 Reliability frontiers
title:
From “more confident”
to “can this update be trusted?”
lede: SAR, RoTTA, and DeYO extend TTA through optimization stability, sample memory, and the sources of confidence. They provide tools, rather than conclusions that directly apply to IRSTD.
body:
The current route is internal learning with TTT

This chapter is retained as a TTA comparison, not the project’s experimental route. The current sequence is original TTT → prototype variant → one IRSTD-specific change. Start with TTT mechanisms or the replication matrix.

SAR · ICLR 2023

Towards Stable Test-Time Adaptation in Dynamic Wild World

For small batches, mixed distributions, and class imbalance, SAR combines reliable-sample selection, sharpness-aware optimization, and recovery. LN/GN avoid dependence on batch statistics, but cannot prevent collapse on their own.

Conceptual objective: minθ Σₓ 1[H(pθ(x)) < H₀] max‖ε‖≤ρ H(pθ+ε(x))
Estimate a local perturbation ε, then update θ using the gradient at the perturbed point

SAM does not simply add an ordinary L2 regularizer; SAR also triggers recovery using a moving average of entropy. Transfer concern: Empty-background images naturally have low entropy, so classification thresholds cannot be copied directly to diagnose collapse; selection may also leave almost exclusively background.

Original sources: SAR · ICLR 2023 ↗

RoTTA · CVPR 2023

Robust Test-Time Adaptation in Dynamic Scenarios

It focuses on which samples drive updates: robust BN, a memory bank considering class balance, timeliness, and uncertainty, and temporal weighting in a teacher–student model to mitigate correlated sampling and distribution changes.

Transfer concern: A class-balanced classification cache cannot simply become equal numbers of foreground and background pixels. Image or patch caches grouped by scene, noise, or candidate quality are possible research directions, but constitute a new design; the cache must contain only current and past samples.

Original sources: RoTTA · CVPR 2023 ↗

DeYO · ICLR 2024

Entropy is not Enough for Test-Time Adaptation: From the Perspective of Disentangled Factors

ŷ = argmax꜀ p꜀(x)
PLPD = pŷ(x) − pŷ(T_destroy(x))

Does the original predicted class become less probable after object structure is destroyed? DeYO combines this signal with entropy for selection and weighting, probing the cues behind high confidence. Both predictions must use the same original pseudo-label index ŷ, rather than subtracting the independently selected maximum probabilities.

Transfer concern: Targets only a few pixels across lack the shape semantics of natural-image objects. Destructive transformations may erase the target or create high-frequency false targets. Candidate-neighborhood perturbations and background replacement are possible research directions, but candidates must not come from test ground truth.

Original sources: DeYO · ICLR 2024 ↗

Compare the three approaches in one research table

MethodMain quantity controlledFirst IRSTD checkAdditional cost
SARLocal gradient stability and recoveryDo empty scenes trigger recovery incorrectly?Additional gradient computation
RoTTASample timeliness and representativenessDoes the cache retain incorrect pseudo-targets?Cache storage and additional training samples
DeYOThe cues supporting high confidenceDoes the destructive transformation remain physically meaningful?Inference on additional views
Locate the failure before choosing components

For low-entropy all-background predictions, inspect the loss and selection first; for order sensitivity, investigate caching and recovery; for drastic output changes under perturbations, investigate optimization stability. Do not stack every component at once, or it will be hard to know what helps.

Pause and test your intuition

DeYO originally predicts target, but background has the highest probability after transformation. What does PLPD compare?

label: 07 TTT inner and outer loops
title:
A hidden state
can itself be a learner.
lede: Use a hand-checkable gradient step to understand internal memory, external supervision and inference boundaries.
body:
One acronym, different questions

Classic TTT prepares an auxiliary self-supervised task during training and uses it to adjust shared features at test time under distribution shifts. TTT layers instead treat a small model’s parameters as sequence state, making internal learning part of representation computation. The ideas are related, but TTT does not universally mean entropy minimization.

RouteWhat learns?Role here
Classic TTT / test-domain adaptationShared features or selected model parametersHistorical and conceptual comparison
TTT layersInner state model W; outer θ controls its inputs and readoutWorking hypothesis and experimental focus

Classic TTT · ICML 2020 ↗ · TTT layers · 2024 / ICML 2025 ↗

Write with K and V, read with Q

Project a token x into a key k, value v and query q. The inner model fW learns a mapping from k to v; q reads a representation from the updated model. W changes with the current sequence. θ contains projections, initialization or other network parameters, as defined by the implementation.

k = θK x, v = θV x, q = θQ x
ℓinner(W) = ½‖fW(k) − v‖²
W′ = W − η∇W ℓinner(W)
z = fW′(q)

This is a teaching form of associative reconstruction. Real layers may add normalization, residuals, token/chunk batching and learned step sizes. It is not a complete implementation, and the inner loss receives no test mask.

Why is the outer loop necessary?

During IRSTD training, predicted masks and training annotations define the outer objective. The outer loop learns useful k/v/q views and how to send the inner readout into a segmentation decoder. It learns how internal learning can help detection, rather than merely minimizing each image’s inner loss.

training image → tokens / projections θ → inner updates of W → dense features → decoder → mask
Lseg(prediction, training mask) → update trainable outer parameters θ

Follow the selected baseline for differentiation through updates, detach boundaries, analytical updates or gradient approximations. Arbitrarily wrapping the whole inner process in no_grad breaks this contract. Inserting a new TTT layer into a trained MiM model does not guarantee useful behavior without training.

Interactive: predict the next gradient step

Start with w₀=0, k=2, v=1, η=0.1 and q=3: the gradient is −2, w₁=0.2 and the readout is 0.6. Increase the learning rate and observe when loss oscillates or grows. Lower inner loss is not evidence of higher detection accuracy.

State lifetime

PhaseOuter θInner WLabels
Source trainingUpdated through the outer task objectiveInitialized and internally trained as the layer specifiesTraining masks supervise the outer task
Single-image inferenceUsually fixedInitialized at image/layer boundaries; prescribed updates runNo test masks
Next independent imageStill fixedReset by default; verify the selected algorithmHeld-out labels belong only to the evaluator

When updates are part of normal TTT computation, disabling them is a mechanism ablation, not the original baseline. Carrying state between independent images also requires an explicit protocol.

From the toy equation to a reproducible model

Record the inner model, initialization, objective, learning rate and steps, projections, token/chunk order, reset scope, precision and gradient path. TTT-Linear uses a linear state model; TTT-MLP uses a nonlinear small network. A richer state model is not automatically faster or more memory-efficient.

Next: why vision cannot simply copy text →

Pause and check your understanding

What do a TTT layer’s inner steps usually update during inference?

label: 08 TTT from text to vision
title:
The same learner,
a two-dimensional problem.
lede: Understand sequence order, position, bidirectional context and dense prediction before choosing visual TTT for IRSTD.
body:
Text order is not image geometry

QuestionAutoregressive textSingle-frame vision
Available contextFuture tokens must not be readThe whole image is usually available; noncausal learning is possible
Sequence meaningA linear token orderFlattened 2D patches; order is a design choice
Required outputNext token or sequence representationSpatially localized dense features for IRSTD
State boundarySequence or documentIndependent image and layer boundaries must be defined

Bidirectional scans, multiple directions and whole-image key/value fitting are possible designs, not universal components of every visual TTT model. Textual causal masks are not mandatory for image detection; future leakage remains forbidden in genuinely causal tasks.

Two similarly named visual candidates

ViT³ / ViTTT studies inner models and inner training for visual TTT, including classification and dense tasks. It is an entry point for studying internal objectives, architectures and optimization choices. Vision-TTT, in the fixed v1 text, uses bidirectional processing and Conv2d for 2D relations and compares CLS placement and pooling. These are different papers, authors and implementations.

ViT³ · arXiv 2025 / CVPR 2026 ↗ · Official ViTTT code ↗ · Vision-TTT · arXiv 2026 v1 ↗

A candidate is not a confirmed baseline

Inner loops, CLS, position encoding and efficiency at resolution 512 identify a family, not a specific implementation. The group model and the meaning of its 76.x score remain unconfirmed. Similar scores do not establish identity.

A classification head is not a segmentation head

image H×W → patch / stem → tokens N×d → TTT → spatial tokens
preserve coordinate mapping → reshape / multiscale features → fixed decoder → H×W probabilities

A CLS vector or globally pooled vector has summarized spatial information. Changing the last classifier to one output channel does not recover pixel locations. First identify each stage’s stride, token grid, special-token removal and positional-embedding interpolation; then attach the segmentation decoder.

Where can a tiny target disappear?

Possible failure points include initial coarse patch compression, repeated downsampling, background-dominated inner objectives and prototype aggregation that removes rare details. A feature-space prototype is not the spatial centroid of a mask component. Trace token coordinates and compare original/prototype responses for small and low-contrast targets.

One hypothesis is to retain a lightweight local path and fuse it with global TTT features. Diagnose the baseline failure first. This general idea is neither a verified gain nor an established novel contribution.

Account for the full computation

With fixed patch/stride: N ≈ (H/p)×(W/p)
Doubling both H and W makes N approximately four times larger

Linear scaling in token count assumes fixed state size, inner steps and other settings. Wall-clock cost also depends on inner gradients, the decoder, memory traffic, kernel fusion and utilization. Report forward/training time, peak memory, precision, batch, tokens and every inner update. A reported high-resolution advantage is not an IRSTD replication result.

Six questions for code handoff

  1. Which paper and commit define the model?
  2. Is W a linear map, an MLP or another state model?
  3. What are the inner objective, learning rate and update steps?
  4. Do prototypes compress inputs, parameterize the inner model or aggregate outputs?
  5. Are spatial tokens retained, and where is state reset?
  6. What task, pretraining, metric and configuration produced the checkpoint?

Apply these questions to IRSTD →

Pause and check your understanding

A model returns only a CLS classification vector. What is the first IRSTD migration step?

label: 09 TTT for IRSTD
title:
Compress information,
keep the faint target.
lede: Use original and prototype TTT as direct controls, then let an observed IRSTD failure motivate one testable change.
body:
The main route: integrate, then compare

B0: original TTT backbone + fixed segmentation decoder
B1: colleague’s prototype TTT + the same decoder
R1: B1 + one IRSTD-specific change

B0 is the direct baseline, B1 transfers an existing method, and R1 tests a new hypothesis. Agree on ownership if prototype v3 or multiscale prototypes are already being developed by a colleague. Keep normal TTT inner updates; a model with updates disabled is not the original baseline.

Domain papers are references, not controlled ablations

MethodUseful ideaComparison boundary
MiM-ISTDLocal words interact with global sentencesWhole-model scores do not isolate a TTT mechanism
IRMambaPixel differences enter state modeling; detail restorationPixel differences are not TTT gradient updates
SAMambaPretrained hierarchical features adapted to infrared tasksSupervised FS-Adapter training is not automatically TTT
MSHNetMultiscale supervision and scale/location sensitivityMasks are used for training and independent evaluation

MiM-ISTD ↗ · IRMamba ↗ · SAMamba ↗ · MSHNet ↗

A falsifiable hypothesis: does compression damage rare foreground?

Hypothesis: background-dominated aggregation may erase rare weak-target tokens. Diagnosis: compare B0/B1 predictions, area-stratified Pd, Fa and empty scenes under the same protocol. Intervention: add only a local-detail path, or change one clearly defined aggregation factor; do not simultaneously change the loss, decoder and multiple hyperparameters.

If B1 does not degrade on small targets, or the intervention only increases false alarms, this explanation is unsupported. Labels may support training and offline diagnosis; the test-time inner objective never receives ground-truth masks. Lower reconstruction loss alone is insufficient.

Fix one dataset and one evaluator first

DatasetInitial roleWhat to freeze
NUAA-SIRSTSuggested small starting pointVersion, file-level train/val/test lists and duplicates
NUDT-SIRSTExpansion after a stable baselineSynthetic-data characteristics, split and target sizes
IRSTD-1kMore scenes and resolutionsVersion, size restoration and annotation conventions

Do not expand to all three datasets in the first week. Select thresholds and checkpoints on validation data, not the test set. Fix probability conversion, connected components and one-to-one matching; define nIoU behavior for empty truth/predictions.

Record more than the best IoU

EvidenceRecord
DetectionIoU, nIoU, Pd, Fa; Fa units and thresholds
Failure groupsTiny area, low contrast, complex backgrounds, empty scenes
Internal computationInner model, steps, learning rate, prototype count and state boundaries
ResourcesFull forward/training throughput, peak memory, device, batch and precision
ReproducibilityCommit, configuration, seed, initialization and checkpoint hash

For whole-model comparisons, list parameter count, pretraining and budget separately. Keep other settings aligned across B0/B1/R1 to interpret the prototype and local-path effects.

Keep TTA in its proper place

Tent, CoTTA and SAR study another set of questions through entropy, teachers and recovery. Their chapters remain conceptual comparisons. The current matrix does not add Tent/SAR as a default next stage; first establish whether TTT internal learning helps single-frame detection.

Open the weekly replication plan and matrix →

What makes B0 and B1 an interpretable first comparison?

label: 10 TTT replication plan
title:
Make one pipeline work,
then ask one question at a time.
lede: A week for handoff, segmentation integration and a first controlled comparison. Exports describe plans, not completed experiments.
body:
This week’s goal and priorities

Goal: run original TTT → integrate single-frame segmentation → compare original/prototype variants. Reading papers is not a completed training run; the exact baseline, weights and inner loop still need handoff. The supervisor should review the hypothesis and division of work.

Replicate the existing method first. Do not simultaneously add a Mamba hybrid, complex multiscale design and TTA updates. If code or resources are unavailable, deliver the handoff sheet and interface design without invented scores.

A working-day schedule

WhenWorkAcceptance evidence
MondayPin original/prototype commits, configs, weights and differencesHandoff sheet, original task and metric meaning
TuesdayForward/backward, spatial features, data and decoderAligned shapes and valid gradients
WednesdayFit a few samples; freeze splits/evaluation; review the ideaTraceable short-run logs and agreed matrix
ThursdayStart B0/B1 with matched settingsSeparate configs, logs and checkpoints
FridayInspect predictions, misses, false alarms and costInterim comparison; unfinished runs marked in progress

Here B2 is a step-count ablation. Give the research chapter’s IRSTD-specific change a separate run identifier rather than conflating two changes. The 256 setting is an initial local protocol, not automatically any paper’s original protocol.

Interactive: choose a stage and export a draft

The export records variables and missing information. It starts no training and promises neither memory use nor accuracy. Before running, supply the source version, data lists, inner-loop and training configurations.

Resources: measure before expanding

Start by requesting one GPU, preferably 40–48 GB of memory; 24 GB can be tried with a small model, input 256 and batch=1. Reserve 24–48 GPU-hours for debugging and short runs. This is a planning allowance, not measured runtime or a fit guarantee. Consider 2–4 parallel GPUs after validation; 8/16 GPUs are not a minimum requirement.

estimated training time ≈ steps per epoch × measured seconds/step × epochs + validation/checkpoint overhead

After warmup, measure 100–200 full training steps including inner updates and decoder, and record peak memory. Ordinary data parallelism does not split one sample’s computation graph automatically. For single-sample OOM, inspect tokens, inner loops and graph retention first.

Shared records and stop conditions

Fix file lists, seed, initialization source, decoder, loss, training budget and evaluator. A first single-seed run diagnoses issues; later repeats are needed for stability claims. If masks are misaligned, gradients break, NaNs appear or a few samples cannot be fitted, debug before long training.

Save IoU/nIoU/Pd/Fa, latency, throughput and memory. For H0/H1, fix hardware, batch, precision and inner steps. Report incomplete runs honestly rather than predicting a gain from an early curve.

Pause and check your understanding

S0 can fit a few training samples. What does this establish?

body:
The current route is internal learning with TTT

This chapter is retained as a TTA comparison, not the project’s experimental route. The current sequence is original TTT → prototype variant → one IRSTD-specific change. Start with TTT mechanisms or the replication matrix.

A minimal 2×2: separate architecture and adaptation gains

Frozen inferenceSame adaptation strategy
CNN / current baselineA: baseline performanceB: adaptation of the existing architecture
Mamba IRSTDC: architecture changeD: combined effect

Compare B−A and D−C to discuss whether adaptation gains depend on architecture; C−A addresses the architecture question. Keep splits, resolution, training budgets, and evaluation code consistent, and report parameter and computation differences. Comparing only D with A does not support attribution.

Interactive: choose state resets and output order

What the exported file means

The JSON is a protocol draft, not a runnable configuration for a training framework. The diagram shows only state transitions, not detection accuracy; A→B→A is a controlled domain sequence composed of single-frame images.

Which choices should an unlabeled loop expose?

# Protocol illustration, not a directly runnable training script
source_state = snapshot(model, optimizer, teacher)
for x in target_stream:  # Access only current and past samples
    if episodic:
        restore_all(source_state)
    if predict_then_adapt:
        prediction = infer(model, x)
    loss = unlabeled_objective(x)  # Does not receive y
    if predetermined_update_rule(loss):
        update_selected_parameters(loss)
        update_teacher_then_optional_restore()
    if adapt_then_predict:
        prediction = infer(model, x)
    save_prediction(prediction)
# A separate evaluator uses held-out labels to compute final metrics.
# Do not use test results to select the best checkpoint.

Per-image resets cover weights, optimizer momentum, the teacher, BN statistics, and caches. Reset TTT-layer inner-loop states at the agreed boundaries. Fix and record initialization, output timing, and update frequency.

Metrics: put units and aggregation in the protocol

IoU = Σ TP / Σ(TP+FP+FN)
nIoU = mean_image [TP/(TP+FP+FN)]
Pd = successfully matched ground-truth targets / total ground-truth targets
Fa_pixel = false-positive pixels / total pixels

For nIoU, specify how empty ground truth and empty predictions are scored or excluded. For object-level Pd, fix the threshold, connected-component definition, center-distance or overlap criterion, and an explicit one-to-one matching rule.

Fa_pixel×10⁶ is the number of false-alarm pixels per million pixels, distinct from false-alarm connected components per image. Report Pd/Fa at a fixed operating point and provide threshold-sweep curves separately for offline analysis. Do not choose the best threshold using test labels and then claim unlabeled deployment.

First-round experiment checklist

DimensionPlanRecord
Methodsource-only → norm entropy → teacher consistencySame θ₀
ParametersSeparate normalization and adapter updates; use full-parameter updates as a comparisonParameter names, counts, and gradients
AblationsAdd or remove EMA, restoration, and candidate weighting separatelyIndependent effects
OrderPer-image resets, accumulation within one domain, A→B→A, and multiple permutationsForgetting and sensitivity to order
Failure groupsLow SCR, small area, edges, defective pixels, and empty imagesPd/Fa and stratified results
RepetitionsA fixed list of seeds and multiple runsMean, variance, or confidence intervals
EfficiencyFixed hardware, batch=1, including all adaptation computationp50/p95 latency, GPU memory, and update frequency

Three ground rules

  1. Do not tune with target labels: choose learning rates, thresholds, and stopping rules on the source validation set or a separate development domain.
  2. Do not look into the future: cache only current and past samples; explicitly distinguish offline adaptation over the full batch.
  3. Do not hide failures: report falling Pd despite lower entropy, increasing Fa on empty images, and forgetting when returning to an earlier domain.

body:
New TTT route: 2025–2026

Read inner models and inner training, then compare spatial processing and dense outputs. ViT³ and Vision-TTT are different papers: candidate reading routes, not the confirmed group baseline.

ViT³: Unlocking Test-Time Training in Vision ↗ · ViTTT ↗ · Vision-TTT: Efficient and Expressive Visual Representation Learning with Test-Time Training ↗

Core papers and additional representative work

VMamba · NeurIPS 2024

VMamba: Visual State Space Model ↗

Focus on: Figure 2 SS2D, Figure 3 final VSS block, and scan ablations.

Tent · ICLR 2021

Tent: Fully Test-Time Adaptation by Entropy Minimization ↗

Focus on: adapted parameters, statistics, and the entropy objective.

CoTTA · CVPR 2022

Continual Test-Time Domain Adaptation ↗

Focus on: the teacher, augmentation trigger, and stochastic restoration.

Mamba · COLM 2024 / arXiv 2023

Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces ↗

Focus on: selection, discretization, and the scan.

Mamba-2 / SSD · ICML 2024

Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality ↗

Focus on: SSD structured matrices and implementation constraints.

SAR · ICLR 2023

Towards Stable Test-Time Adaptation in Dynamic Wild World ↗

Focus on: selection and recovery triggers.

RoTTA · CVPR 2023

Robust Test-Time Adaptation in Dynamic Scenarios ↗

Focus on: the memory bank, robust BN, and dynamic protocols.

DeYO · ICLR 2024

Entropy is not Enough for Test-Time Adaptation: From the Perspective of Disentangled Factors ↗

Focus on: PLPD and destructive transformations.

TTT layers · ICML 2025 / arXiv 2024

Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States ↗

Focus on: the relationship between inner and outer loops, and state models.

MiM-ISTD · TGRS 2024

MiM-ISTD: Mamba-in-Mamba for Efficient Infrared Small Target Detection ↗

Focus on: inner and outer Mamba, local detail, and efficiency.

IRMamba · AAAI 2025

IRMamba: Pixel Difference Mamba with Layer Restoration for Infrared Small Target Detection ↗

Focus on: PDMamba, layer restoration, and noise ablations.
